planting.note: Divide clumps in early spring or right after flowering, replanting in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Spilled Milk carries an unusually heavy overlay of silver across nearly the whole leaf blade, leaving only a thin ring of green at the margin, as though a puddle of milk had been poured across each leaf and stopped just short of the edge.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where the heavily silvered leaves will hold their pale color without scorching. Small funnel-shaped flowers open coral-pink from the bud in earliest spring and shift to violet-blue as they mature, often showing both colors together on the same cluster before the foliage has fully expanded. Once flowering finishes the rounded, felted leaves enlarge to cover the crown, forming a dense, luminous patch that reads almost solid silver from a few feet away and brightens a dim corner more than the spotted-leaf types. Water during dry spells, since the thin leaves wilt quickly in drought, and shear off tattered foliage in mid-summer to encourage a fresh flush for fall.

planting.note: Divide established clumps after flowering or in early fall, setting divisions into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Samurai belongs to the narrow-leaved longifolia group, which generally blooms a few weeks later and tolerates summer humidity better than the broad-leaved saccharata cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Samurai produces long, narrow, blade-like leaves densely dusted with silver spotting that fuses into a near-continuous metallic sheen down the center, giving the clump a sleeker, more upright, sword-like texture than the rounder-leaved lungwort cultivars. Clusters of small, funnel-shaped flowers open coral-pink and mature to violet-blue in early to mid spring, held just above the emerging foliage. The narrow leaf form sheds heavy rain more readily and tends to resist powdery mildew better than broad-leaved types through humid summers. Keep soil evenly moist and mulch to cool the roots, since the strappy foliage flags quickly if the ground dries out.

planting.note: Divide congested clumps in early spring or after bloom, replanting into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Silver Streamers was selected within the longifolia group for exceptionally slender, almost grass-fine leaves that add a distinct fine-textured accent among the typically broad-leaved lungworts.

directions: Plant in evenly moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Silver Streamers sends up tufts of unusually long, thin, arching leaves brushed almost end to end with silver spotting that merges into streaking bands, giving the clump a fountain-like, fine-textured look quite different from the broad, rounded foliage of most lungwort cultivars. Small, funnel-shaped flowers open pink and age to blue-violet in early spring, held on short stems just above the emerging leaf tufts. The narrow foliage sheds moisture well and generally stays cleaner through humid summers than broad-leaved types, making it a useful textural contrast planted among hostas, hellebores, and ferns. Keep the soil from drying out fully, since the thin blades wilt fast under drought stress.
